13317.take: One big game on seven targets doesn't make him a reliable starter, and two short touchdowns inflate the line. Still, the Bucs' receiver pecking order looks open with Egbuka slumping and a possible backup quarterback, so he's worth a modest waiver bid for the 7-2 redraft team as a bench stash, not a Week 12 starter. In dynasty he's a young receiver with a growing role, which fits the rebuild; buy or add him cheaply before he strings together more games.

11557.name: Joe Milton
11557.headline: Eagles' starter struggles again before Thanksgiving trip to Dallas
11557.news: Philadelphia put Jalen Hurts on injured reserve with a blood clot in his calf on Oct. 17, and signed Milton off Dallas' practice squad soon after, initially as a third-string QB behind Tanner McKee. Milton has since become the starter. He threw for 169 yards and ran for 64 in Week 9 (13.16 half-PPR, per Sleeper), and after the Week 10 bye he went 11 of 21 for 141 yards and no TDs with 7 rushing yards in the Nov. 22 win over Pittsburgh (6.34). His legs give him some fantasy floor, but he isn't a 1QB option for the 7-2 redraft team, even against a Dallas defense that allows a lot of points. In superflex dynasty, he's young and cheap, and starts like these give his arm talent a chance to show, so a 1-8 rebuild can stash him at little cost as a backup QB with some upside. 6806.headline: Suspended one game by Broncos; already lost lead job to Coleman

6806.take: Before the suspension he was already a low-snap backup, so the fantasy impact is mostly that his role is now even less secure; at least one outlet questions whether he plays for Denver again this season. He's droppable in 12-team redraft unless you're deep at bench spots and want insurance on Coleman, which is now shaky insurance. In dynasty he's 27 with a long injury history and now a discipline issue, so a 1-8 rebuild should move him for anything, though the market will be very thin. Don't drop him in dynasty just to make room unless you need the roster spot.
